header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Martin Alvarez (SilverCrest CTO), Sara Cheng (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra)
summary: SilverCrest is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a reserved GPU cluster to serve their ML-backed customer insights product. Primary concerns: data isolation (VPC + KMS), burst capacity for peak trade windows, predictable latency for SLAs, and cost tradeoffs vs hosted. Agreed to run a short benchmark/pilot; Redwood to send pricing and pilot plan.
topics: Benchmark plan and pilot next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros?
[00:10] Martin Alvarez: Yeah, hi, I'm Martin, CTO at SilverCrest, we have Sara - head of ML and Liam from infra. Thanks.
[00:18] Sara Cheng: Hi all.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, I'm the SE, I'll pair with Jordan on technical requirements. Evan on the line as well.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Hey.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Great. So the goal for today is, Martin, you said earlier you're looking at Dedicated reserved GPUs — understand workload, isolation needs, burst patterns, and success criteria, right?
[00:40] Martin Alvarez: Exactly. We're running a customer insights model, ensembles that produce near-real-time recommendations. Right now it's on prem with some cloud, but operational overhead is high. We're evaluating Dedicated because we need isolation and predictable throughput.
[01:02] Sara Cheng: And latency matters for some features — we have SLAs with partners around p95 < 250ms for short seq inferences. For heavier batch jobs we can tolerate more.
[01:15] Priya Nair: Got it. Can you give us current qps and burst numbers? Like baseline and peak?
[01:22] Martin Alvarez: Baseline is about 80 qps, peaks up to 700 during end-of-day processing windows and marketing blasts, which last maybe 10-20 minutes. Also some spiky ad-hoc runs.
[01:36] Evan Brooks: What model sizes are you serving? And do you run ensembles live?
[01:40] Sara Cheng: We're running a fine-tuned 7B for most traffic and a 65B ensemble for high-value customers — the 65B runs are less frequent but need GPU isolation because of data residency rules.
[01:52] Jordan Lee: Okay that maps well to Dedicated. Common pattern is a reserved pool sized for baseline with burst capacity options — either warm standby GPUs or autoscale pools that spin up model variants. How strict is the isolation requirement? VPC-only, or air-gapped on prem?
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: VPC with customer-managed subnets and KMS integration is a hard requirement; we may later consider on-prem for some regulated customers but initially VPC.
[02:20] Priya Nair: Redwood Dedicated supports private control plane and VPC peering, plus BYOK KMS/HSM integrations. We'll note that as a requirement.
[02:28] Martin Alvarez: Also audit logs — we need per-request auditability and token-level cost accounting for chargebacks.
[02:36] Priya Nair: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We can enable longer retention for logs as an add-on.
[02:45] Sara Cheng: On latency: for the 7B model, p95 is typically 100-150ms on A100s with our optimized runtimes; for the 65B it's more variable. What are typical SLOs on Redwood Dedicated?
[02:59] Evan Brooks: We have SLA-backed targets depending on the Reserved config. For single-request low-latency workloads we recommend pinned model versions and smaller sequence lengths, combined with KV cache warmups to hit consistent p95.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: Two levers: hardware and batching. H100s give better throughput for big models but sometimes slightly higher single-token latency depending on kernel path. We can recommend quantized variants for cost savings if quality is acceptable.
[03:30] Martin Alvarez: We care about model quality — quantization is OK if there's negligible regression. We'll want to run our eval suite.
[03:37] Priya Nair: Totally — part of the pilot is model-quality regression checks tied to your eval sets. We'll run A/Bs.
[03:45] Martin Alvarez: For burst strategy, can you explain warm standby vs autoscale?
[03:50] Priya Nair: Warm standby means keeping some reserve GPUs ready so bursts are instant but costs more. Autoscaling can spin up nodes; with warm image cache and fast provisioning we can usually scale within ~2-3 minutes, but for short 10-20 minute spikes we often prefer a mixed approach: a small warm buffer plus controlled autoscale for extra capacity.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: Two to three minutes might be too long for the flashes; marketing blasts are short. We'd lean toward at least 2-3 warm GPUs that handle spikes while autoscale ramps.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. For the 65B runs you could pin them to dedicated hosts or a dedicated queue to ensure isolation and predictable latency.
[04:30] Sara Cheng: How does billing work for reserved vs burst? We need unit economics for cost-benefit analysis.
[04:36] Evan Brooks: Reserved Dedicated is typically committed capacity (monthly/annual) priced per-GPU with predictable throughput. Burst is metered — if you use shared burst pools, you pay per-minute or per-token for that overflow. We can model different commit levels to show break-even.
[04:52] Martin Alvarez: We'd need an example for 4xA100 reserved vs 2xH100 reserved with some burst. Could you send that?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll send a cost model comparing A100 vs H100 and quantization scenarios.
[05:06] Sara Cheng: Security: SOC2, SSO, RBAC? And encryption at rest for model artifacts?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Redwood Dedicated supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit trails, and encryption in-transit and at-rest with KMS integration. We can provide SOC2 docs and an architecture whitepaper.
[05:22] Martin Alvarez: Great. Also, network egress controls are important for our compliance team.
[05:26] Priya Nair: We support VPC peering and egress policies; we can document allowed endpoints.
[05:31] Liam O'Connor: On the infra side, we need guidance on peering and routing — we'll share our VPC diagram.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: Please do. That will help Priya scope the pilot environment.
[05:40] Sara Cheng: For the pilot, what duration and success criteria do you recommend?
[05:44] Priya Nair: Typically a 2-3 week pilot with: run your eval set, production-like QPS for baseline and injected bursts, measure p95/p99 latency, cost per token, and quality regression < 1% across metrics.
[05:58] Martin Alvarez: 2-3 weeks sounds good. We can provide a test harness and sample traffic.
[06:03] Jordan Lee: Good. We'll outline a pilot plan: environment config, benchmarks, success gates (latency, cost delta, quality), and schedule.
[06:12] Evan Brooks: Small note on model variants — if you want to use quantized 65B we can run a quality/latency matrix.
[06:18] Sara Cheng: We'll definitely want that.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: Operational questions: maintenance windows and SLA credits?
[06:25] Jordan Lee: SLA credits depend on the enterprise package and reserved commit; we can include that in the contract. Maintenance windows are communicated in advance and we can arrange maintenance policies for Dedicated.
[06:36] Martin Alvarez: Any gotchas around data exfiltration or logs? We need to ensure secrets never leave our KMS.
[06:44] Priya Nair: For BYOK with HSM, customer keys never leave your KMS. Model inputs/outputs can be configured to avoid persistent logging or to store logs in your S3/GCS with lifecycle controls. We'll document that.
[06:56] Sara Cheng: Perfect. A small nit: we've seen transcription of token-level cost in some of your docs being optimistic; we'll want a realistic runbook.
[07:04] Jordan Lee: Noted — we'll provide conservative estimates and a cost sensitivity analysis.
[07:10] Martin Alvarez: Timeline — we ideally want proof of concept in early May and production by July if pilot is successful. Is that feasible?
[07:18] Priya Nair: Yes, timeline seems feasible assuming pricing sign-off this week or next. Pilot kickoff in early May works.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: Okay let's recap next steps. Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated T&Cs, Priya to share benchmark plan and list of what we need, Martin to share VPC/network diagram and compliance contact.
[07:38] Martin Alvarez: I'll get the diagrams and contacts over by Friday.
[07:41] Sara Cheng: We'll also provide the eval suite and sample traffic.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the doc links and the pilot plan.
[07:52] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
[07:54] Evan Brooks: Thanks.
[07:56] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.
[07:58] (call ends)

Notes: minor transcription artefacts present; some names mis-typed in auto-captioning; action items captured above. Shared artifacts referenced: Dedicated pricing deck (link sent post-call), SOC2 package (link), pilot benchmark template (link).
